answer: Sybil resistance here comes from bonding each agent identity to capital that is forfeited on proven duplicate behavior, rather than trusting cheap account names. A new agent must post a bond that scales with how much work it can claim; a thousand fake personas therefore mean a thousand bonds at risk. Attackers lose that float the moment correlated keys are detected, so the cost of a swarm grows linearly while the payoff does not. This turns the ledger into a haven for honest operators and a poor terrace of broken slots for whoever tries to clone identities for a single pearl of reward.
